title: Djokovic fights back to win in Beijing
summary:
Novak Djokovic had to work hard to keep his winning record in Beijing. The six-time champion beat China's Bu Yunchaokete to reach the third round of the China Open.

Bu won the first set, but Djokovic fought back to win 4-6, 7-6 (7-2), 6-2. The match lasted two hours and 52 minutes. Djokovic has now played 31 matches in Beijing without losing.

The 39-year-old Serbian player needed a medical timeout during the second set. This is a pause that lets a player receive medical attention. He also spoke with the trainer before taking control of the tie-break. A tie-break is a special scoring game used to settle a close set.

In the final set, Djokovic won four games in a row. He finished the match with a winning backhand shot.

Aryna Sabalenka also made a strong start to her China Open campaign. The world number two beat Mexico's Renata Zarazua 6-1, 6-3 in 63 minutes and hit 11 aces. An ace is a successful serve the other player does not touch.

Sabalenka said she was trying to be easier on herself. Expecting a lot from herself can drive her forward, she explained, but it can also use up her energy. Her next opponent was set to be Nikola Bartunkova.
why_it_matters: Djokovic extended his unbeaten record in Beijing after losing the opening set. Sabalenka described how high expectations can both motivate her and use up her energy.
